title: Exchange Rate Tolerance on Single-Use Card Purchases: Casebook — Pocketwire Visa Debit Card
content:
**Rule.** This rule covers the Pocketwire Visa Debit Card. On a purchase made with a single-use virtual card and disputed as an incorrect amount, the exchange rate tolerance is:

- **2.5 percent**, when the purchase is foreign and settled 3 or more calendar days after the card's latest authorization;
- **1.0 percent**, when the purchase is foreign and settled fewer than 3 calendar days after the card's latest authorization;
- **0 percent**, when the purchase is domestic.

A purchase is foreign when it was processed outside the United States or in a foreign currency, as recorded on the purchase. The card's latest authorization is the most recent authorization hold on the single-use card. The days run from its date to the purchase's settlement date.

### Cases (hypothetical dates)

| Purchase | Latest authorization | Settled | Calendar days | Exchange rate tolerance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| foreign | 1 June | 4 June | 3 | 2.5 percent |
| foreign | 1 June | 3 June | 2 | 1.0 percent |
| foreign | 1 June | 1 June | 0 | 1.0 percent |
| foreign | 1 June | 11 June | 10 | 2.5 percent |
| domestic | 1 June | 9 June | 8 | 0 percent |

*The 3-day edge.* Settlement exactly 3 calendar days after the latest authorization is "3 or more", so the tolerance is 2.5 percent. Settlement 2 days after is fewer than 3, so it is 1.0 percent.
